name: Bank Reconciliation
title: Bank Reconciliation
answer: Bank reconciliation is the process of matching transactions recorded in a company's cash ledger against the bank statement for each bank account, then explaining any difference. It covers deposits, withdrawals, fees, interest, chargebacks, returned payments, and timing items such as outstanding checks or deposits in transit. In treasury and liquidity work, the scope extends to multiple accounts, currencies, and payment rails, and to the daily cash position that depends on those balances. The output is a reconciled set of balances with clear support for every open item, not just a zero difference.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the accounting or ERP system of record, bank connectivity through host-to-host links, APIs, or statement files such as BAI2, MT940, and CSV exports. A reconciliation engine or module ingests both sides, normalizes dates, amounts, references, and counterparties, and stores the matched and unmatched items in a controlled database. Where remittance data arrives as email or PDF, optical character recognition and document parsing feed the same pipeline. Access is usually role based, with separate permissions for importing bank data, proposing matches, and approving adjustments.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method starts with data ingestion and normalization, then applies deterministic rules for exact matches on amount, date, and reference. Fuzzy matching and machine learning models handle partial references, split deposits, and one-to-many matches, while anomaly detection flags unusual amounts, duplicate payments, or unexpected fees. Exceptions are routed to a preparer who codes them to the general ledger, and a reviewer approves the reconciliation and the adjusting entries. The audit trail records the source data, the match logic, the model version where one is used, and the human decision.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk and provenance turn on who can see bank data, who can change a match, and what evidence supports each reconciled balance. Controls include segregation of duties between preparer and approver, restricted access to bank credentials, encryption of statement data, and retention rules for reconciliation evidence. Model risk management applies when machine learning proposes matches or classifies exceptions, so teams document training data, performance thresholds, and fallback to manual review. Provenance means every balance can be traced back to a bank statement line and a ledger entry, with a clear record of any override.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward continuous reconciliation, where bank feeds and payment APIs update cash positions throughout the day rather than at month end. More accounts and instant payment rails increase the volume of exceptions, which pushes teams toward automated exception handling and real-time monitoring. Agentic workflows may assemble evidence, propose journal entries, and route approvals, but human sign-off remains the control point for material adjustments. The practical goal is a faster close with fewer unexplained items and a stronger audit trail, not the removal of the accountant from the process.
